\section{Haar-normalized tails}\label{sec:tails}

Normalization need not be estimated numerically: Proposition~\ref{prop:character}
gives $\int p_t\dd H=1$ exactly.  Let $\Pr_t$ denote the probability measure
on $\SU$ with density $p_t$ relative to normalized Haar measure.  Combining
\eqref{eq:image} with \eqref{eq:haar-radial} cancels one sine denominator.

\begin{theorem}[Explicit normalized tail]\label{thm:tail}
Let $0<\rho<\pi$ and $t>0$.  Define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:E}
E(t)=t\frac{e^{-\pi^2/(2t)}+e^{-2\pi^2/t}}
{1-e^{-4\pi^2/t}}.
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:tail}
\Pr_t\{\theta\ge\rho\}
\le e^{t/2}\sqrt{\frac2\pi}\,t^{-3/2}
\left[t\left(\rho+\frac{t}{\rho}\right)e^{-\rho^2/(2t)}+E(t)\right].
\end{equation}
The right-hand side may be replaced by its minimum with one.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The zero-image radial numerator is bounded using $\sin\theta\le\theta$ and
extension to infinity:
\[
 \int_\rho^\pi\theta\sin\theta e^{-\theta^2/(2t)}\dd\theta
 \le\int_\rho^\infty\theta^2e^{-\theta^2/(2t)}\dd\theta
 \le t\left(\rho+\frac t\rho\right)e^{-\rho^2/(2t)}.
\]
The last inequality is the elementary Mills-ratio bound.  All nonzero images
contribute at most $E(t)$ in absolute value.  Multiplication by
$(2/\pi)C_t=e^{t/2}\sqrt{2/\pi}\,t^{-3/2}$ and exact normalization finish the
proof.  Appendix~\ref{app:tail} gives the image integration details.
\end{proof}

At fixed $\rho$, \eqref{eq:tail} has logarithmic rate
$-\rho^2/(2t)$ as $t\downarrow0$; the nonzero images are exponentially
smaller when $\rho<\pi$.
